foxai.n102: Change Project Task List Storage Location
foxai.n108: Clean Up Fox AI Junk Files
foxai.n117: Which model service to use. Local services need no API key.
foxai.n118: API base URL (leave empty to use the selected provider's default). Must include the version prefix, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
foxai.n119: Model name (leave empty to use the provider's default model)
foxai.n120: Plaintext API key (not recommended). Prefer the command `Fox AI: Set API Key`, which stores the key in the system keychain.
foxai.n121: Base system prompt (tool-usage rules are appended automatically in agent mode)
foxai.n124: Timeout (ms) for a single streaming request. Non-streaming requests automatically get at least 90s, since reasoning models return only after full computation.
foxai.n125: Max number of history turns sent to the model
foxai.n126: Automatically attach the current file and selected code when asking
foxai.n127: Force non-streaming requests (return the full result at once). **Use this when your network/proxy makes streaming requests fail with `Parse Error`.** The trade-off is no character-by-character typing effect.
foxai.n128: Streaming response parse format. If the provider's Content-Type is non-standard and streaming shows no output, force a format here. `jsonl` also supports MCP's Streamable HTTP transport.
foxai.n129: Relax HTTP response parsing (`insecureHTTPParser`). Enable when a proxy returns malformed response headers causing `Parse Error`. Leave off unless streaming keeps failing.
foxai.n130: Image attachment send strategy. `auto` blocks plain-text models like deepseek-chat to avoid the server error ``unknown variant `image_url` ``.
foxai.n131: **Models forced to be treated as vision-capable** (substring match, case-insensitive). When `auto` wrongly classifies a vision model as plain text, add the model name or a fragment here, e.g. `Qwen3.6`, `my-custom-vl`. Takes priority over auto-detection.
foxai.n132: **Models forced to be treated as non-vision** (substring match, case-insensitive). When `auto` wrongly classifies a plain-text model as vision-capable and causes a 400, fill it in here. Takes priority over auto-detection but is lower than `foxAi.visionModels`.
foxai.n133: Max rounds of images kept in history (older images are replaced with text placeholders to save bandwidth and tokens)
foxai.n134: Max size per attachment (MB); larger files are skipped
foxai.n135: Allow the model to call web search tools (the plugin searches and feeds results to the model; no native search support required)
foxai.n136: Third-party search API key (only needed when provider is tavily/serper)
foxai.n138: Give a pair of eyes to **plain-language models without vision**: when the main model cannot read images, it automatically sends the image to the configured "second multimodal model", which describes what it sees as text, then hands that back to the main model to continue reasoning. Ideal when the main model is plain text (e.g. deepseek-chat, qwen-coder) but you want it to understand images.
foxai.n139: Preset for the second multimodal model (optional). Leave as custom to use the baseUrl/model/apiKey below. Options: openai / gemini / grok / mistral presets, or custom.
foxai.n140: API base URL for the second multimodal model, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1 or local Ollama http://localhost:11434/v1. Must support OpenAI-compatible chat (with image_url) or Responses (input_image).
foxai.n141: API key for the second multimodal model (leave empty for local models)
foxai.n142: Second multimodal model name, e.g. gpt-4o, llava, qwen2.5-vl, or other vision-capable models
foxai.n143: API protocol for the second multimodal model. chat = OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions (image_url); responses = OpenAI Responses API (input_image).
foxai.n145: Open a dedicated image-generation channel for the **main controller agent** (parallel and opposite to "multimodal vision relay"): when the main model (plain text is fine) decides an image is needed, it calls the configured "dedicated image model" to generate it and renders it in the chat. The image model is fully isolated from the main chat model. Ideal for models like Qwen wan2.1-image, DALL·E.
foxai.n146: Preset for the image model (optional). Leave as custom to use the baseUrl/model/apiKey below. Options: openai / gemini / grok / mistral presets, or custom.
foxai.n147: API base URL for the image model, e.g. https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1 (Qwen) or https://api.openai.com/v1 (DALL·E). Must support OpenAI-compatible chat (image generation response).
foxai.n148: API key for the image model (leave empty for local models)
foxai.n149: Image model name, e.g. wan2.1-image, dall-e-3, or other image-capable models
foxai.n150: API protocol for the image model. chat = OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions; responses = OpenAI Responses API.
foxai.n151: Max tokens for the image request (some models ignore this; leave default)
foxai.n152: Image request timeout (ms). Image generation is usually slower than text; default 60s, adjust per model.
foxai.n154: Security audit governance: whether to allow the self-audit agent (security_audit) to run `npm audit` dependency checks over the network. **Default false = network-isolated sandbox** (never makes outbound requests, never reads .env / .aws / .ssh / *.pem credential files; matched secret values are masked in the report). Set true only when dependency vulnerabilities are truly needed and the environment is trusted.
foxai.n156: Enable MCP remote tools. Default off: keep pure local CLI tools, load no MCP server-exposed tools.
foxai.n157: Custom install directory for @modelcontextprotocol/sdk. Leave empty to use the default user-home/.fox-ai/mcp-modules (e.g. C:\Users\yourname\.fox-ai\mcp-modules). If installed via setup-mcp.js --prefix <dir> or the foxAi.setupMcpDeps command chose a custom location, set this to the same directory so the extension can load the SDK.
foxai.n158: Priority strategy when tool names collide. Default local-first (CLI first, MCP fallback). Namespaced MCP tools (mcp__<id>__<name>) are unaffected and always exist independently.
foxai.n159: Whether to auto-inject MCP remote tools into the agent's available tool list (so the AI decides when to call). Default false: the model cannot see MCP tools and can only call them explicitly via /mcp <server> <tool> [JSON params] in chat. Set true to restore the old behavior — the AI auto-selects and uses MCP tools.
foxai.n160: (Experimental) Auto-import and connect VS Code's native mcp.json MCP servers into Fox AI: they appear as manageable entries in the Fox AI manager (the agent can also call them) and the corresponding read-only cards are hidden. Deletion is one-shot — it also cleans the matching entry in VS Code mcp.json (auto-backed up to .foxbak before writing back). Set false to fall back to read-only display, no connection, no linked deletion.
foxai.n161: (Experimental) Connect Playwright MCP so the agent can read web pages / accessibility trees in the background. Requires @modelcontextprotocol/sdk and @playwright/mcp installed and a browser downloaded (npx playwright install). Enabling launches a Playwright MCP server process in the background.
foxai.n162: (Experimental) Generic MCP server list to connect any standard MCP server without coding. Each item: { id, transport?:'stdio'|'sse', command?, args?, url?, env?, enabled?, flat?, headers? }. stdio example: { id:'filesystem', command:'npx', args:['-y','@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem','/path'] }; sse example: { id:'remote', transport:'sse', url:'http://localhost:8000/sse' }. Tools are exposed as mcp__<id>__<toolName>.
foxai.n163: (Security) Additional whitelist for commands allowed to launch MCP servers. By default only npx/npm/pnpm/yarn/bun/deno/node/uvx/python/python3/pipx/docker/podman are permitted; to use other commands you must add them explicitly here.
foxai.n164: (Security) Whether to allow MCP servers to connect to intranet / localhost / link-local addresses (SSRF protection). Default false: rejects 127.0.0.0/8, 10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16, 169.254/16, localhost, etc. Enable only when an intranet server truly exists.
foxai.n165: (Security) Whitelist of sensitive environment variable names allowed to pass through verbatim when launching MCP servers. By default variables whose names contain token/secret/password/api_key/private_key/aws/auth are stripped to avoid leaking local secrets to child processes.
foxai.n167: Session save directory (leave empty to use the extension's global storage). After changing, new sessions are saved to the new location; old sessions are not migrated automatically.
foxai.n168: Long-term memory file save directory (leave empty to use the global storage memory/ directory). Existing memories are migrated automatically after changing.
foxai.n169: User skills save directory (leave empty to use the global storage user-skills/ directory). Existing skills are migrated automatically after changing.
foxai.n170: Project task list file save directory (leave empty to use the global storage root). Existing tasks are migrated automatically after changing.
foxai.n171: Enable local knowledge base: before each question, retrieve relevant snippets from local docs and inject them into context
foxai.n172: Knowledge base directory or file path list, supports markdown / txt / jsonl
foxai.n173: Max characters injected into context per retrieval
foxai.n175: Enable AI organizing: when on, the agent's knowledge-base retrieval only reads the "organized" directory; the original text never enters context (the agent reads the organized content).
foxai.n176: List of original document directories to be organized by the AI (supports md/txt/code/logs/etc). Originals stay here and are never injected into context.
foxai.n177: Output directory for organized Markdown. Leave empty to default to C:\Users\asis\.fox-ai\knowledge\, which the agent's knowledge-base retrieval reads. Customizable, but must be a path the agent can read.
foxai.n178: AI service for organizing. ⚠️ Strongly recommend a local AI (llama.cpp / Ollama / LM Studio) so data never leaves your machine; if you choose a cloud service, organizing sends source file contents to its server (key is stored only in local SecretStorage).
foxai.n179: Custom Base URL for the organizing AI (leave empty to use the provider default).
foxai.n180: Model name for the organizing AI (leave empty to use the provider default). A long-context model is recommended for organizing.
foxai.n181: Custom organizing prompt (leave empty to use the built-in template: structured Markdown — Summary / Key Points / Important Details / Tags).
foxai.n182: Enable "context-overflow auto-compression": when context usage exceeds a threshold, automatically compress earlier conversations into summaries with the organizing AI and write them to "Knowledge Base-2"; the agent then continues via local knowledge-base retrieval while immediately shrinking context.
foxai.n183: Compression trigger threshold (fraction of the context window). E.g. 0.9 means compress only when usage exceeds 90%. Depends on foxAi.contextWindow being set correctly (otherwise the percentage cannot be determined).
foxai.n184: How many recent conversation messages to keep after compression (the rest are compressed into Knowledge Base-2).
foxai.n185: Knowledge Base-2 directory (where compression summaries are stored). Leave empty to default to C:\\Users\\asis\\.fox-ai\\knowledge-2\\, which the agent's knowledge-base retrieval reads; customizable but must be readable by the agent.
foxai.n186: Use BM25 scoring for knowledge-base retrieval (instead of pure keyword match) to improve relevance
foxai.n187: Number of most relevant chunks returned by RAG retrieval
foxai.n189: Cache project scan results (tech stack / file roles / dependencies) to avoid re-scanning the workspace every tool call
foxai.n191: Allow the agent to create/update the project task list and display it in the chat panel
foxai.n192: AI service used to auto-summarize task goals (leave empty to use the current chat model)
foxai.n193: Custom Base URL for the summarizing AI (leave empty to use the provider default)
foxai.n194: Model name for the summarizing AI (leave empty to use the provider default)
foxai.n196: Absolute path to the node executable (leave empty to use node from PATH). Used to auto-run node --check syntax validation after writing JS files.
foxai.n197: When on, after writing/changing a code file an AI model runs an extra strict review (syntax / logic bugs / runtime errors / security leaks). Default off.
foxai.n198: Provider ID for the review model (leave empty to use the current chat provider). Options: llamacpp / ollama / deepseek / zhipu / qwen / kimi / siliconflow / openrouter, etc.
foxai.n199: API base URL for the review model (leave empty to use that provider's default). Local models can use http://localhost:11434.
foxai.n200: Model name for the review model (leave empty to use that provider's default). A local lightweight model is recommended to save tokens.
foxai.n202: Show the "Context Usage" entry in the chat panel, displaying real-time estimated tokens and proportions of each prompt component.
foxai.n203: Model context window size (tokens). Set 0 to hide the percentage and show only the estimated token count; common values: 128000, 200000, 32768, 8192.
foxai.n205: Override the auto-approve tier (leave empty to use foxAi.agent.autoApprove). The Harness uses this to decide whether read/write/execute/download/install/calling external extensions need confirmation. off = all require confirmation; all = all automatic.
foxai.n206: Sensitive path blacklist (regex or path fragment). Files matching a "write" operation are forcibly blocked and never written. By default protects .env / .ssh / id_rsa / *.pem / credentials / wallets / known_hosts, etc.
foxai.n207: Dangerous command blacklist (regex or fragment). Matches are forcibly blocked, e.g. rm -rf /, format C:, shutdown, dd if=, diskpart, mkfs, etc.
foxai.n208: Whitelist (command IDs) of external extension commands Fox AI may call. Defaults to foxAi.bridge.allowedCommands.
foxai.n210: Allow the AI to read files outside the workspace (using absolute paths). When off, out-of-workspace reads like read_file / list_dir / open_file are rejected.
foxai.n211: Extra confirmation level when modifying or deleting files outside the workspace.
foxai.n212: Default starting directory for global search (scope=global). Leave empty to use the user home directory.
foxai.n214: Enable agent mode: allow the AI to read/write workspace files, run terminal commands, and read diagnostics. When off, degrades to pure Q&A.
foxai.n215: Plan-and-Execute confirmation mode: for multi-step tasks the AI first lists a complete plan and submits it; it executes only after you confirm. To adjust the plan during execution it must call revise_plan with a reason and be confirmed again before continuing.
foxai.n216: Automatic code review (Code Review sub-agent): after writing code (edit_file/write_file/delete_file succeeds), automatically run a read-only review sub-agent on the change, show its comments in chat and feed them back as observations to help reduce low-level errors.
foxai.n216a: Review injection timeout (ms): before the main agent outputs its final answer, wait up to this many milliseconds for the review sub-agent. If the review finishes in time, its feedback is injected into the system prompt for the main agent; otherwise the agent answers first and the review card appears later with a one-click apply button. 0 means don't wait.
foxai.n218: Max consecutive tool-call steps per task (hard cap to prevent infinite loops burning tokens). Exceeding it pauses and (if auto-compression is on) compresses context.
foxai.n219: Max times to auto-send "continue" and re-call when a single reply is truncated by length limit (finish_reason=length/incomplete). 0 disables auto-continue.
foxai.n220: Front routing gate: simple knowledge-base Q&A skips the agent main loop and is answered directly via RAG to save tokens. Only meaningful after enabling the knowledge base.
foxai.n221: Max question length (characters) judged as a "simple query" by the routing gate; longer ones go through the agent main loop as usual.
foxai.n222: Scalpel-style tool trimming: when on, only the few tools most semantically relevant to the current question are injected into the system prompt (other tools can still be called normally and are not disabled), saving ~30% of tool-description token cost. Default off; try small-scale first.
foxai.n223: Max number of "relevant tools" injected per round by the dynamic subset (excluding always-resident core tools). Larger = more complete but more tokens.
foxai.n224: Comma-separated tool-name whitelist always injected regardless of relevance (e.g. mcp__fetch__fetch-url). Core read/write/execute/retrieve/time-sensitive tools are already resident; no need to repeat here.
foxai.n225: Mandatory citation & provenance guardrail: requires content based on knowledge base / files / search / code to carry a [source] marker; when retrieval or sources lack basis it must explicitly say "insufficient information" and forbid fabrication. Default off.
foxai.n226: Plan-execute separation: at task start, one lightweight call splits the requirement into a step list with dependencies/parallelism (DAG), decoupling thinking from execution to avoid long-chain "think-while-doing" errors. Default off.
foxai.n227: Planner-specific provider (leave empty to use the main model). Options: openai / deepseek / custom, etc.
foxai.n228: Planner-specific baseUrl (leave empty to use the main model address).
foxai.n229: Planner-specific model name (leave empty to use the main model). A low-cost model is recommended.
foxai.n230: Max tokens for a single planner generation.
foxai.n231: Planning mode: auto = enable automatically only for multi-step tasks (via local heuristic rules), always = plan for every task, off = never plan. Default auto.
foxai.n232: Planner request timeout (ms). Default 30000 (30s); planning failure auto-degrades to direct execution.
foxai.n233: Self-Consistency double verification: for high-risk tool calls (execute/write/delete/code review/security audit), before execution ask the model to reason again at a different temperature; if the two decisions disagree, pause and prompt for human review. Default off.
foxai.n234: List of tool names requiring double verification; leave empty to use the built-in high-risk set (run_command/edit_file/write_file/delete_file/security_audit/review_changes).
foxai.n235: Sampling temperature for the second reasoning pass (higher = more diverse). Default 0.8.
foxai.n236: Global tool timeout circuit breaker: wrap each tool call in a unified hard timeout; on timeout throw an error to switch paths; maintain a per-tool breaker counter and skip the call after consecutive failures hit the limit. Default off (when enabling, raise timeoutMs first).
foxai.n237: Hard timeout in ms for a single tool call; on timeout interrupt and prompt to switch paths. Default 30000 (30s).
foxai.n238: Consecutive failures for the same tool that trigger the breaker (skip call, prompt to switch paths); auto half-open recovery after 60s cooldown. Default 3.
foxai.n239: Tool calling protocol. llama.cpp needs --jinja to support native function calling.
foxai.n241: Shell used for background execution (leave empty for auto: cmd.exe on Windows, $SHELL elsewhere)
foxai.n242: Max duration (ms) for a single command; auto-terminated on timeout
foxai.n243: Command blacklist (regex). Built-in already blocks high-risk commands like rm -rf /, mkfs, shutdown, etc.
foxai.n244: Max characters of a single tool result sent back to the model
foxai.n245: Hard cap on total conversation history characters; oldest messages are dropped when exceeded (prevents unbounded memory growth when auto-compression is off)
foxai.n246: Require the model to prefer structured JSON/YAML for summaries, plans, and task lists to reduce redundant natural language
foxai.n247: Attach a code skeleton (function/class signature summaries) when injecting project context, helping the model locate quickly without reading whole files
foxai.n249: Enable inline code completion (gray ghost text); recommended with code models like qwen2.5-coder
foxai.n252: How many lines backward to use as context
foxai.n253: Inject project structure/skeleton context during inline completion, consistent with the chat AI
foxai.n254: Max project-context characters injected per completion (too large may increase latency and token cost)
foxai.n256: Default install root for runtimes (Python/Node/C-C++/C#/Java/Go/Rust). Installer mode still writes to user PATH; archive mode extracts directly here. **Ensure the path is under your control and does not pollute the system drive.**
foxai.n258: Elevation policy when installing runtimes that need admin rights (e.g. .NET / rustup).
foxai.n259: **Whitelist of other extension commands Fox AI may call.** Only commands listed here can be invoked by Fox AI. Empty default = all forbidden.
foxai.n260: Whether whitelisted commands skip secondary confirmation (audit logs are still recorded). Recommended to keep off.
